source_row.rationale: Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state is characterized by severe hyperglycemia, hyperosmolality, and profound dehydration from osmotic diuresis, often with neurologic changes. Option B is correct. The measured glucose and hyperosmolality exclude hypoglycemia and water intoxication, and fasting ketosis does not produce this extreme hyperglycemic hyperosmolar picture.
source_row.source_detail: HHS diagnostic criteria/clinical presentation: severe hyperglycemia (typically glucose >=600 mg/dL), hyperosmolality, and profound dehydration with minimal significant ketoacidosis; cognitive changes can accompany marked hyperosmolality. 2024 international consensus report, Diabetes Care 47(8):1257-1275; currentness live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Reduction of Risk Potential: diagnostic/laboratory interpretation, postprocedure monitoring, device management and potential complications. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

source_row.stem: A dehydrated client has a glucose level of 650 mg/dL, markedly elevated effective serum osmolality, and altered mental status. Which condition is most consistent with this pattern?
